macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall as hotter inflation raises Fed hike fears
items.summary: The Dow fell about 0.3%, the S&P 500 0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite 0.7% on Tuesday after October CPI rose 0.4% month over month, above the 0.3% forecast. Technology stocks underperformed, with Nvidia down roughly 5.5%.
items.source: The Wall Street Journal via Economic Times

items.title: Fed officials signal possible December rate hike
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller backed a quarter-point increase in December and said a half-point move should be considered if inflation remains elevated. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan also called for at least two further quarter-point increases.

items.title: Treasury yields jump after inflation report
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.99% from 4.88%, while the two-year yield posted a sharp increase as traders priced in greater odds of additional Federal Reserve tightening.

items.title: Anthropic sets terms for proposed IPO
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed plans to offer 825 million shares at an indicated range of $70 to $78 per share, implying proceeds of up to roughly $64.4 billion and a fully diluted valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market sells off as Bitcoin falls below $74,000
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $73,796, down 2.1% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 3.8% to about $2,053. The broader crypto market capitalization declined roughly 3.1% amid higher-than-expected U.S. inflation data and leveraged liquidations.[3][8]

items.title: $178 million in leveraged long positions liquidated
items.summary: A broad crypto-market decline triggered approximately $178 million in long-position liquidations, adding to selling pressure and volatility.[1]

items.title: MARA sells 13,597 Bitcoin and repays $750 million debt
items.summary: Bitcoin miner MARA disclosed the sale of 13,597 BTC, reportedly worth about $1.1 billion, to repay $750 million in debt. The company also authorized a $500 million share buyback and said two data-center leases could be delayed until 2027.[3][4]

items.title: FinCEN action puts pressure on MEXC
items.summary: MEXC said it contacted the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network through outside counsel after FinCEN issued a restriction order identifying the exchange as a primary money-laundering concern. Binance said it would stop processing fund transfers involving MEXC and related entities.[3]

items.title: Germany considers including crypto accounts in financial-monitoring system
items.summary: A German Finance Ministry draft reportedly proposes extending the country’s account-inquiry system to encrypted accounts and allowing temporary freezes of up to five business days.[6]

items.title: South Korean lawmaker calls for scrapping planned crypto tax
items.summary: Opposition lawmaker Song Eon-seok urged South Korea to abolish, rather than further delay, its planned cryptocurrency income-tax regime. The government and ruling party have proposed postponing implementation from 2027 to 2029.[7]

items.title: NYSE explores Avalanche for tokenized-stock settlement
items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange is reportedly working with Avalanche on its planned tokenized-stock platform. Robinhood separately said it does not oppose its shares being traded on OKX’s tokenized-stock platform.[4][3]

items.title: Security researchers flag malicious code in Bee-js and Swarm Desktop
items.summary: Socket researchers reported that malicious code was inserted into Ethersphere’s bee-js package and Swarm Desktop application, with the apparent aim of targeting wallet keys.[3]

items.title: Ethereum Foundation sells 2,000 ETH
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation reportedly sold approximately 2,000 ETH, worth about $4.14 million, through CoW Swap over two days.[6]

items.title: Sei governance proposal passes amid market decline
items.summary: Sei’s SIP-6 Autobahn governance proposal reached quorum and passed with roughly 1.9 billion SEI votes in favor. SEI nevertheless fell about 4.1% during the broader market selloff.[8]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic announced updated versions of its Fable and Mythos models, claiming up to 30% faster performance and 20% lower cost than earlier versions. Fable includes stronger safeguards for broad availability, while Mythos is restricted to vetted cybersecurity and biomedical organizations.

items.title: Google announces new TPU chips for AI agents
items.summary: Google introduced the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, specialized AI processors designed respectively for confidential computing and long-context workloads. The chips are intended to support increasingly agentic AI systems and are expected to arrive next year.

items.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Carbon availability and unveils Robotics 2.5
items.summary: Google reportedly made its Gemini 4 Carbon model available to additional users and introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, aimed at improving robots’ ability to perform complex tasks. The company also highlighted a cybersecurity use case involving the discovery of a zero-day vulnerability.

items.title: Meta introduces Muse Ember for high-volume agent tasks
items.summary: Meta announced Muse Ember, a smaller model designed for repetitive workloads such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long-document parsing. The company says it delivers competitive intelligence at a lower per-task cost.

items.title: Adobe and Disney agree to develop custom AI models
items.summary: Adobe signed a multiyear agreement with Disney to build custom models trained around Disney characters and visual styles. The planned applications span theme parks, film, and ESPN.

items.title: Fireworks reports security breach affecting customer data
items.summary: Open-source AI hosting company Fireworks confirmed a hack that exposed billing information and parts of some customers’ models and datasets. The disclosure comes as the company reportedly prepares a major fundraising effort.

items.title: AI-powered quantum error-correction system reports preliminary gains
items.summary: Quantum X Labs said its AI-based quantum error-correction technology produced up to 20% fewer logical decoding failures in preliminary tests using data from IBM quantum processors. The program has expanded to three IBM systems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony reportedly cancels Fairgames live-service shooter
items.summary: Sony has reportedly canceled Fairgames, Haven Studios’ planned multiplayer heist shooter, after testing produced mixed feedback and retention missed targets. Haven is expected to support other PlayStation studios, with no layoffs reported.

items.title: GTA 6 development reportedly completed ahead of launch
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said Rockstar has completed development on Grand Theft Auto VI, which is scheduled for November 19. He also said preorders are running far ahead of expectations.

items.title: Xbox says GTA 6 set Microsoft Store preorder record
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Grand Theft Auto VI has set a record for the most preorders of any game on the Microsoft Store and Xbox Store. Microsoft also has a newly reported 10-year partnership with Take-Two.

items.title: Logitech gives employees paid gaming day ahead of GTA 6
items.summary: Logitech announced a paid “Game Day” benefit for its roughly 7,000 employees and interns, allowing each worker to take one day off to play a game. The company also plans a livestreamed gaming event on GTA 6’s launch day.

items.title: SAG-AFTRA backs organizing efforts by Rockstar developers
items.summary: SAG-AFTRA publicly expressed support for Rockstar Games workers organizing ahead of a union vote. The statement frames the effort as part of a broader push for stronger worker representation in the games industry.

items.title: German games industry objects to proposed EU youth-safety rules
items.summary: The German Games Industry Association criticized the proposed EU KIDS Act, arguing that it could weaken existing game-specific safeguards and age-rating systems. The group said established PEGI and USK protections should not be undermined by broader social-media regulation.
